newsitem.title: POLAND: Warsaw bourse outlook hazy next week after surge.
newsitem.headline: Warsaw bourse outlook hazy next week after surge.

text.p: The Warsaw bourse surged this week, setting three consecutive 33-month highs, but analysts were not sure whether the rally would continue next week.
They said profit-taking was likely early in the week, but were unsure whether the market, buoyed by foreign buying, would hit new records or fall later in the week.
The WIG index soared 6.4 percent this week to 15,418.9 points.

"I don't think it's a longer growth as it's too violent and seems to be purely psychological, not based on fundamentals, but it's still difficult to say when it will end," said Pawel Tarnowski of Raiffeisen Capital and Investment Polska.
Analysts said investors would be watching December and 1996 inflation data due on Wednesday, as the central bank has said a possible decision to raise rates might hinge on those figures.
They said data on food price growth in January's first 10 days, due on Friday, would also interest inflation watchers. But if the main market fell, 15,000 points should provide strong support.

Analysts said aggregate enterprise results for the January-November period due on Tuesday, and data on industrial and construction output in December due on Friday, were unlikely to move the market in the short-term.
They said companies' December earnings reports and preliminary 1996 data, which start flowing late next week, could help some stocks extend this week's gains.

Analysts said PPABank's 1.25-million-share rights issue next week and the 1.2-million-share offer by construction firm Bauma SA, starting on Monday and Thursday respectively, were too small to draw significant capital from stocks.
Construction firm Mostostal Krakow SA and rubber company Stomil Sanok SA enter the bourse's main market on Tuesday and Thursday respectively.

Analysts said Mostostal Krakow, which had no initial public offering, could start trade between 10 and 14 zlotys, but some said a debut over 15 zlotys was possible. Sanok is expected to start trade well above its issue price of 25 zlotys.
Indykpol moves its shares from the parallel to the main market on Monday.
Analysts could not explain the surge by the week's top gainer, Mostostal Warszawa, up 24.1 percent, but some said the growth was likely caused by foreign demand.
Rafako surged 20.6 percent after it said it was seeking a strategic investor, analysts said.
Some said ComputerLand's 9.4 percent fall was accidental while others said it represented profit-taking after the stock rose for most of the fourth quarter.
